title: performance(canary): enhanced auto-detection and rollout guards for latency/throughput regressions
author: Maya Thompson
description: Add statistically robust automated detection of latency and throughput regressions to the perf-canary pipeline and introduce rollout guards that block model rollouts when regressions exceed configured thresholds. Motivation: customers continue to hit silent perf regressions after model rollouts; we need an automated guard that prevents degrading changes from reaching production without manual inspection. Changes include: 1) new detection algorithm (rolling baseline with bootstrap CI + p95/p99 drift checks), 2) configurable rollout policy integration (block/allow/warn) exposed to deployment config, 3) metrics pipeline adjustments to include synthetic warmup traces and GPU-utilization tagging, 4) e2e perf-canary harness and smoke tests for rollout gating, 5) small refactor of the perf-canary state machine to support pending/blocked states. The description below documents design decisions and operational notes. Design: use a rolling 24h baseline with exponential decay, compute bootstrap CIs for p95/p99 and throughput; flag regressions when regression magnitude > relative_threshold AND the lower-bound of the new observation CI exceeds the baseline upper-bound by configured alpha. This reduces false positives on noisy workloads. Rollout guards: integrate with deployment orchestrator to mark rollouts as "blocked" and surface reasons to the Console. Guards can be overridden by a staged canary percent and manual override; overrides require a Linear ticket and an audit log entry. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is opt-out for existing deployment configs. Migration: new config schema added (perf_canary: {enabled, sensitivity, window_hours}). Testing: unit tests for statistical detection, simulated canary runs with synthetic traces, and integration tests that exercise the block/unblock flow. Operational notes: added alerting to PagerDuty for blocked rollout events and a Console banner for affected routes. See linked Linear cards for rollout policy and observability follow-ups.

release_notes: Add automatic performance canary detection (bootstrap CI) and rollout guards that block model rollouts on verified latency/throughput regressions. Configurable sensitivity and window; opt-out by default for existing deployments.
notes_for_ops: Blocked rollout events create PagerDuty incidents and Console banners. To override a block, update the deployment config with staged canary percent or follow the runbook in docs/runbooks/perf-canary-rollout-guards.md and reference a Linear ticket.
